# Conclusion {#sec-conclusion}

Forecasting under censored demand remains one of the most persistent and under-addressed challenges in supply chain operations. In FPSC, where stockouts, service interruptions, and incomplete reporting are structural features rather than anomalies, failing to correct for demand censorship distorts observed data and undermines both forecast accuracy and downstream public health outcomes.

In this study, we proposed the TCKF, a state-space forecasting method tailored for censored demand. By distinguishing between partial and full censorship, dynamically inflating process uncertainty, and incorporating conformal prediction for distribution-free intervals, the TCKF offers a robust and adaptable solution suited to real-world FPSC environments.

We extended traditional forecast evaluations by linking prediction performance to inventory outcomes using a unified economic objective that explicitly weights the severe, asymmetric penalty of stockouts against the burden of excess inventory. Evaluated across a comprehensive suite of deterministic and uncertainty-aware inventory policies, TCKF consistently achieved reliable service provision while maintaining efficient stock levels, successfully overcoming the severe overstocking or instability observed in current benchmarks.

Crucially, we quantified how improvements in forecasting translate into public health outcomes. Compared to existing practices, TCKF reduced contraceptive stockouts and associated user loss without resorting to overstocking, demonstrating both operational and ethical value in resource-constrained settings.

Taken together, our findings underscore the importance of jointly addressing demand censorship and inventory integration in forecasting models. While developed for contraceptive supply chains, the TCKF framework is readily applicable to broader public health and humanitarian supply chains where lost demand is common but rarely modelled. It represents a step toward more context-aware, decision-relevant forecasting in complex operational environments.
